primary_source.title: Language Models are Few-Shot Butlers
primary_source.access: Read the official ACL PDF through the web tool; no local PDF checksum or reproduction of the paper's experiments is claimed.

source_checks: Section 2.2, printed page 9313: action modeling maximizes the likelihood of action tokens rather than the entire trajectory.
Section 2.3, printed page 9313: IAM starts with an expert-demonstration-trained language model, collects environment interactions, and further trains with action modeling on successful trajectories.
Section 3.2, printed page 9314: the paper implements the procedure with GPT2-medium in ALFWorld after initial expert training.
decision: The new citation and chronological description are supported. The draft correctly declines to introduce successful-trajectory training as a new method. Expert initialization and action-only supervision themselves also have direct precedent here; the narrower shared-checkpoint comparison does not by itself establish methodological novelty.
remaining_work: Broader literature coverage and institution-specific citation formatting remain pending. Different models, protocols and task distributions prevent direct numerical comparison with this thesis.
actions: Read the primary PDF and current chapter, hash the chapter, and write this independent review. The chapter and scientific artifacts were not modified; no model, environment or experiment was run.
